title: DARPG organises 20th National e-Governance Webinar on Government Process Re-engineering for Digital Transformation
subtitle: AgriStack and e-Jagriti, National Award-winning initiatives, showcase technology-enabled transformation in agricultural governance and consumer dispute resolution
body_text:
The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) organised the 20th National e-Governance Webinar (NeGW) under the theme “Government Process Re-engineering by use of technology for Digital Transformation (Central Level)”. The webinar was chaired by Shri Avanish Kumar Mishra, Joint Secretary, DARPG.
The webinar showcased two National Award-winning initiatives recognised under the Central Level Initiatives category of the National Awards for e-Governance 2026 — AgriStack of the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and e-Jagriti of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs. The initiatives demonstrated how technology-enabled process re-engineering can improve efficiency, transparency, accessibility and citizen-centric service delivery.
The following award-winning initiatives were presented:
AgriStack: Dr. Pramod Kumar Meherda, Additional Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, presented the Gold Award-winning AgriStack initiative. AgriStack is a Digital Public Infrastructure initiative aimed at modernising agricultural governance and service delivery across the country.
AgriStack is built around three core registries — the Farmers’ Registry, Crop Sown Registry and Geo-referenced Village Maps — providing a digital foundation for verified farmer identification, land holdings and crops sown. The initiative follows a federated architecture, with the registries created, owned and managed by States and Union Territories while ensuring interoperability across the national agricultural ecosystem.
The Digital Crop Survey is operational across 31.36 crore plots in 648 districts, while more than 10 crore unique Farmer IDs have been created and 5.52 lakh geo-referenced village maps have been completed. Farmer IDs are also being integrated with major programmes including PMFBY, PM Asha, MahaDBT and MSP Procurement.
AgriStack demonstrates how technology-driven process re-engineering can strengthen transparency, enable verified delivery of government schemes and reduce dependence on fragmented and manual processes.
e-Jagriti: Shri G. Mayil Muthu Kumaran, Deputy Director General, National Informatics Centre, presented the Silver Award-winning e-Jagriti initiative, which demonstrates how digital platforms can transform consumer dispute resolution.
e-Jagriti establishes a unified national digital ecosystem for consumer dispute resolution across the National, State and District Consumer Commissions. The platform replaces fragmented legacy systems with a standardised, end-to-end digital workflow covering online filing, digital scrutiny, payment processing, hearings, orders and disposal of cases.
The platform also integrates virtual and hybrid hearings, automated cause lists, real-time notifications, analytics dashboards and mobile application support, enabling consumers and other stakeholders to access and manage consumer dispute resolution processes digitally.
The initiative has transformed traditionally paper-based and time-consuming processes into a seamless digital experience, reducing physical visits and manual dependency while improving transparency, accessibility and efficiency in consumer dispute redressal.
The webinar witnessed participation from senior officials across approximately, 1200+ Officials, including Central Ministries, State Governments, District and Local Bodies, administrations from across the country and officials of DARPG.
At the conclusion of the webinar, Shri Hari K Bhatt, Deputy Secretary, DARPG, delivered the Vote of Thanks. He thanked the speakers and participants and encouraged States, Districts, Local Bodies and Central Ministries to examine the showcased initiatives for adoption and replication in their respective areas of governance.
The webinar reaffirmed the importance of technology-enabled Government Process Re-engineering in transforming public service delivery and strengthening efficient, transparent, accessible and citizen-centric governance.
*****
NKR/Anand

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

enrichment.summary: DARPG held its 20th National e-Governance Webinar on Government Process Re-engineering for Digital Transformation, showcasing two Central Level Award-winning initiatives from the National Awards for e-Governance 2026 — AgriStack (Ministry of Agriculture) and e-Jagriti (Ministry of Consumer Affairs). AgriStack, built on three federated registries (Farmers' Registry, Crop Sown Registry, Geo-referenced Village Maps), has created over 10 crore Farmer IDs and covers 31.36 crore plots across 648 districts. e-Jagriti provides a unified digital platform for consumer dispute resolution across National, State and District Consumer Commissions, integrating online filing, virtual hearings and analytics dashboards.
enrichment.context:
AgriStack is part of India's broader Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) push, similar in philosophy to Aadhaar, UPI and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, aiming to create verified, interoperable digital identities and records — in this case for farmers, their landholdings and crops. Its federated architecture, where states own and manage registries while ensuring national interoperability, reflects India's evolving model of cooperative digital federalism in agriculture, and is meant to enable targeted, leakage-free delivery of schemes like PM-KISAN, PMFBY, PM-AASHA and MSP procurement by linking beneficiary identity to verified crop and land data. e-Jagriti, meanwhile, builds on the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the e-Courts mission mode project's philosophy of judicial digitisation, aiming to reduce pendency and improve access to consumer grievance redressal by digitising the entire lifecycle of a consumer dispute case.

The National Awards for e-Governance, instituted by DARPG, recognise successful digital governance initiatives for replication across Central, State and District levels, and the periodic National e-Governance Webinar series is DARPG's mechanism for disseminating best practices among officials nationwide. While the webinar itself is a routine knowledge-sharing event, the underlying initiatives — particularly AgriStack's scale and its role as an agricultural DPI — are relevant to aspirants tracking India's digital governance and agricultural reform landscape.

prelims_questions.question: AgriStack, a Digital Public Infrastructure initiative in agriculture, is built around which of the following three core registries?
options: Farmers' Registry, Crop Sown Registry, Geo-referenced Village Maps
Land Records Registry, Irrigation Registry, Market Price Registry
Farmers' Registry, Soil Health Registry, Weather Data Registry
Crop Insurance Registry, MSP Registry, Farmer Bank Account Registry
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, AgriStack's digital foundation consists of the Farmers' Registry, Crop Sown Registry and Geo-referenced Village Maps, created and managed by States/UTs in a federated architecture.

prelims_questions.question: e-Jagriti, showcased at DARPG's National e-Governance Webinar, is a digital platform primarily associated with which domain?
options: Consumer dispute resolution across Consumer Commissions
prelims_questions.explanation: e-Jagriti, developed under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, provides a unified digital ecosystem for consumer dispute resolution across National, State and District Consumer Commissions.

mains_questions.question: Discuss how Digital Public Infrastructure initiatives like AgriStack can transform agricultural governance in India. What challenges must be addressed for such federated digital systems to succeed?
Examine the role of technology-enabled Government Process Re-engineering in improving citizen-centric public service delivery, with reference to examples such as e-Jagriti.

study_notes.reason: AgriStack provides a genuinely testable factual core (registries, scale, integration with schemes) while also serving as a case study for analysing India's Digital Public Infrastructure model in agriculture; e-Jagriti and the webinar itself are largely administrative and lower-value.

prelims.point: AgriStack is built on three federated registries: Farmers' Registry, Crop Sown Registry, and Geo-referenced Village Maps
prelims.why_important: UPSC could test the specific composition of AgriStack's architecture as a factual item, especially given its DPI significance.

prelims.point: AgriStack has created over 10 crore Farmer IDs and covers 31.36 crore plots across 648 districts under Digital Crop Survey
prelims.why_important: Scale figures could appear in statement-based questions on flagship digital agriculture initiatives.

prelims.point: AgriStack follows a federated architecture where registries are created, owned and managed by States/UTs while ensuring national interoperability
prelims.why_important: This distinguishes AgriStack's model from centralised DPIs like Aadhaar, a distinction UPSC favours testing.

prelims.point: Farmer IDs under AgriStack are being integrated with PMFBY, PM-AASHA, MahaDBT and MSP Procurement
prelims.why_important: Links a digital identity system to specific scheme names, a common factual-linkage question format.

prelims.point: e-Jagriti is a unified digital platform integrating National, State and District Consumer Commissions under the Consumer Protection Act framework
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of the three-tier consumer dispute redressal structure and its digitisation.

prelims.point: DARPG's National Awards for e-Governance recognise initiatives for replication across Central, State and District levels
prelims.why_important: Institutional fact about DARPG's award mechanism that could appear in a matching-type question.

mains.point: AgriStack exemplifies India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) approach extended to agriculture, aiming to link verified farmer identity with land and crop data for leakage-free scheme delivery
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a Discuss/Examine question on how DPI models like Aadhaar and UPI are being replicated in agricultural governance and their expected impact on subsidy leakage and targeting.

mains.point: Federated architecture of AgriStack reflects a cooperative digital federalism model where states retain ownership of registries while enabling national interoperability
mains.analytical_use: Helps answer questions on Centre-State coordination challenges in implementing pan-India digital governance systems.

mains.point: e-Jagriti's digitisation of the consumer dispute lifecycle addresses pendency and access issues in consumer grievance redressal, paralleling e-Courts reforms
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions on use of technology to improve access to justice and reduce case pendency in tribunal-like bodies.

mains.point: Government Process Re-engineering (GPR) using technology is positioned as a means to improve transparency, efficiency and citizen-centric service delivery
mains.analytical_use: Provides a generic analytical frame for 'how technology improves service delivery' type questions, illustrated via concrete cases.

both.concept: AgriStack as a federated Digital Public Infrastructure for agriculture
both.prelims_angle: Composition of its three registries, scale figures, and scheme integrations can be tested as factual statements.
both.mains_angle: Its federated model and DPI philosophy allow analysis of digital governance's role in targeted delivery, data ownership, farmer privacy, and Centre-State cooperation in agricultural reform.
